articleTitle: Investigation of optical loss and bandwidth of InP-organic hybrid optical modulator
abstract: We numerically investigated the performances of EO polymer optical modulator with InP slot waveguide on III-V-OI wafer. It is found that an InP slot modulator shows 30 times smaller optical loss than a Si slot modulator when designed for the same modulator bandwidth. We also numerically presented that an InP-organic hybrid optical modulator shows clear eye opening at 100 Gbps NRZ owing to 10 dBm improvement in optical modulation amplitude.

articleTitle: CVD Growth of BN Thin Films using B2H6
abstract: CVD growth of BN thin films using B2H6 was investigated. BN growth was conducted at a susceptor temperature of 1360°C, pressure of 100 mbar under H2 carrier gas. Wrinkle patterns were clearly observed by atomic force microscopy. The X-ray diffraction and Raman scattering spectroscopy confirmed (002) / (004) and E2g mode of h- BN. Thickness and optical constants of h-BN were determined by fitting the variable angle spectroscopic ellipsometry spectra. The indirect bandgap of 5.61 eV was estimated from Tauc's plot.

articleTitle: Effects of thermal annealing on film quality of InAs-On-Insulator structures fabricated by Smart Cut method
abstract: We study the characteristics of InAs-On-Insulator (InAs-OI) substrates fabricated by the Smart Cut method, which combines wafer bonding with splitting by H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantation. Annealing at 400 °C for 1 h is significantly effective for recovering damages in the InAs layer induced by H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implantation, which is evaluated by Raman spectroscopy and Hall measurements. It is revealed that the InAs layer still has a high electron density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{x}10^{18} \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$</tex>, which is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> times higher than that of the donor InAs wafer and that the interface between InAs and the BOX layer also has accumulated electrons with a high areal density of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7\mathrm{x}10^{12}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex>. The operation of ultra-thin-body (UTB) InAs-OI nMOSFETs fabricated by the Smart Cut method is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Interface engineering of Sn-based oxide semiconductors
abstract: Electron transport at the oxide semiconductor interfaces has attracted much attention for emergence of two-dimensional transport and field-effect operation. In the Sn-based oxides, a perovskite BaSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> is recently investigated as a candidate for transparent conducting oxide because of the high-mobility of electron in the widely-extended Sn 5s based conduction band. In addition, corundum derivative structure LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> can also host B-site Sn-based oxides such as ZnSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and MnSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. We fabricated BaSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films on SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrate by pulsed-laser deposition. To prepare ZnSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films, we applied LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrate with molecular-beam epitaxy. Field-effect transistors based on both films show large on/off ratio > 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. In this talk, thin films fabrication and the interface engineering of BaSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and ZnSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> will be discussed for the improvement of interface quality and superior performance of field-effect transistor with these films.

articleTitle: Crystal structures of GaAs/GaNAs core- multishell nanowire
abstract: Introduction of several % of N into GaAs can provide large variability in lattice constant and band gap. The introduction of heterostructure into the nanowire provides intentional carrier control within the ststem, showing the possibility for the realization of advanced electronic devices. In this study, we report the results of X - ray diffraction (XRD) and electron back scattered diffraction (EBSD) investigation on the structural properties of GaAs - based core - multishell nanowires with GaNAs shell layer prepared by molecular beam epitaxy. The introduction of N into the GaNAs shell showed the peak shift of zinc-blende (ZB) related XRD GaAs (111) peak to the high angle side, indicating the strain deformation of the entire nanowire. In addition, the N introduction reduces the intensity of the wurtzite(WZ)-related GaAs (0002) peak. The phenomenon was further investigated by EBSD. As a result, the WZ structures have smaller diameter than ZB phases, suggesting the transformation of WZ structure to ZB by the introduction of GaNAs shell

articleTitle: Processing of GaN vertical devices: Static Induction Transistors
abstract: In this presentation we will see how vertical GaN devices have made progress over the last decade. Beyond CAVET and MOSFET, we are observing very interesting device performances in more simple geometry device like Static Induction transistor (SIT). We will focus on the recent advancement made in SIT development. Lack of avalanche continues to stay as an issue that although observed and reported in GaN devices, is not yet a routine phenomenon. We will discuss key issues in device processing that we have to overcome to enable a viable path into next-generation power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Deep-Level Defect Investigation of Si-Doped $\beta$-Ga2O3 Homoepitaxial Films Grown by Halide Vapor Phase Epitaxy
abstract: We have electrically investigated deep-level defects in Si-doped <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> homoepitaxial films grown by halide vapor phase epitaxy (HVPE), employing capacitance-voltage (C-V) and steady-state photo-capacitance spectroscopy (SSPC) techniques. The optical bandgap was determined to be ~4.6 eV from Tauc plots. From differential 1/C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-V plots, the effective n-type carriers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{d}}-\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{a}}\vert)$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 4.2\mathrm{x}10^{16}\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$</tex> were seen to be almost uniformly distributed. SSPC measurements revealed four positive deep-level defects (T1, T2, T3, T4, and T6) with their optical onsets at ~1.77, ~2.45, ~2.78, ~3.18, and ~3.88 eV below the conduction band and two negative deep-level defects (T5 and T7) with their optical onsets at ~3.67 and ~4.0 eV above the valence band. In particular, the ~3.67 eV and ~4.0 eV levels were found to be significantly enhanced compared to those in undoped <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrates and are probably attributable to oxygen vacancies produced by Si doping into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> epitaxial films during the HVPE growth. In addition, the ~3.88 eV level with precipitous photo-capacitance change is likely associated with dislocations and/or surface defects <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> homoepitaxial films.

articleTitle: Spin-dependent quantum emission from defects in hexagonal boron nitride
abstract: Optically addressable spins associated with localized defects in wide-bandgap semiconductors are the basis for rapidly expanding quantum technologies in nanoscale sensing and quantum information processing. Whereas most research has focused on three-dimensional host materials such as diamond, the van der Waals material hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) has emerged as a robust host for bright, stable, room-temperature quantum emitters (QEs). I will discuss recent experiments that reveal the role of spin for QEs in hBN. Select QEs exhibit striking, anisotropic modulation of emission in response to an applied magnetic field, consistent with optical dynamics featuring a spin-dependent inter-system crossing between singlet and triplet spin states. Many questions persist regarding the chemical and electronic structure of these QEs, which generally exhibit widely heterogeneous optical characteristics, and ongoing work aims to elucidate their formation and stabilization mechanisms. Nonetheless, the discovery of optically addressable spins in room-temperature h-BN ushers in a new platform for spin-based quantum technologies with the potential for atom-scale engineering and versatile functionality.

articleTitle: High-Performance In0.53Ga0.47 As FinFETs for logic and RF Applications
abstract: We demonstrate the beneficial effects of advanced MOS interfacial technique using PEALD treatments on the electrical performance of In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</inf>As FinFETs. The devices exhibit gm, max of 3.8 and Q of 40.4 at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{ds}}=0.5\ \mathrm{V}$</tex>, which are the record values among III-V and Si-based FETs. These results are attributed to the superior high-k/III-V MOS interface quality achieved by the PEALD treatments and volume inversion effect in the small dimension. This is boosting the performance and potential of III-V MOSFETs toward its limitation for next-generation of logic/RF CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Quantification of external quantum efficiency for near-band-edge emission of $h$-BN bulk crystals under photo-excitation
abstract: The external quantum efficiency (EQE) of radiation was quantified for the near-band-edge emission of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-BN bulk crystals under photo-excitation by using an integrating sphere. The maximum EQE values was as high as 4% and this value is unexpectedly large, though <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-BN is an indirect material. This may be caused from the efficient scattering of indirect excitons assisted by phonons (LO(T)/TO(T) for 5.77-eV emission, and LO(T)/TO(T) + 2TO(K) for 5.51-eV emission). Furthermore, such the phonon-assisted scattering processes bring the photo emission energy lower than the fundamental absorption edge energy (~5.8 eV) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-BN, and therefore, the light extraction efficiency can become very high resulting into the high EQE.

articleTitle: Emergent transport phenomena in MBE-grown 2D materials and their heterostructures
abstract: Since the discovery of graphene, a family of layered materials with nanometer-scale thickness named ‘2D materials’ and their heterostructures have become an invaluable material platform for condensed matter research, providing intriguing properties and functionalities that are missing in their bulk counterparts. Those researches on 2D materials have been mainly done with mechanically-exfoliated nano-thick crystals from ‘top-down’ approach due to its simplicity and wide applicability, while materials under investigation have been limited to cleavable and thermodynamically-stable compounds. We have been developing a growth process of 2D materials based on ‘bottom-up’ molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE), which potentially broadens the scope of materials even to hardly cleavable and thermodynamically-metastable compounds. In this presentation, we will introduce our growth recipe in detail, and present our recent achievements in transport studies including 2D superconductivity and 2D magnetism, as well as development of van der Waals heterostructures exhibiting intriguing interface transport phenomena.

articleTitle: Growth of high-quality GaN single crystals using the Flux-Film-Coated Na flux LPE (FFC-LPE) method
abstract: The Flux-Film-Coated Na flux Liquid-Phase-Epitaxy (FFC-LPE) method was developed for the growth of high-quality GaN single crystals. Although conventional Na flux method enables us to grow large GaN single crystals with low dislocation density, uneveness of growing surface take a lot of inclusions. In the FFC-LPE method, epitaxial growth proceeds in the flux film which covers on the seed GaN template to keep flat surface.

articleTitle: InGaAs Quantum Dot Dual-Band Photodetector of Bipolar Photocurrent
abstract: We report a dual-band photodetector grown by molecular beam epitaxy. The device epi-structure includes a GaAs PN- and an InGaAs quantum dot PIN-photodetector in a two-terminal, back-to-back configuration. At room temperature, the photocurrent-voltage characteristics show a serpentine curve. Under zero bias, a positive photocurrent is detected as the optical wavelength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda)=530$</tex> nm of incident light, and a negative photocurrent for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda=950\ \text{nm}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Switching and HTRB characteristics of Highly reliable GaN MOS-HFET
abstract: The GaN MOS-HFET we have proposed could significantly reduce the maximum electric field of the MOS gate to 1/3 when the high reverse bias is applied. With this effect, High Temperature Reverse Bias (HTRB) characteristics were greatly improved compared with a conventional MOS-HFET. The device with saturation current exceeding 60 A are fabricated and good switching characteristics are also reported in the paper.

articleTitle: Coherent control of a GaAs quantum dot spin qubit operated in a feedback loop
abstract: Single electrons in quantum dot structures confined by electrostatic gating offer a unique platform for quantum information processing. However, spin coherence is easily disturbed by various types of noise in the host semiconductor material. We utilize a feedback-control technique to compensate nuclear-spin noise in a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure and demonstrate 30-fold enhancement of spin coherence time. We find that the noise affecting the microwave-driven spin coherence shows a 1/f spectrum in this regime, which is universally found in most of semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: Hydrogen in semiconducting oxides
abstract: Hydrogen does not exist as a neutral impurity in semiconductors; it always gives up an electron becoming positively charged impurity or acquires an electron becoming negatively charged impurity. This has profound effects on the electronic properties of materials.

articleTitle: (010) $\beta$-Ga2O3 Metal Oxide Catalyzed Epitaxy (MOCATAXY) growth and Sn doping in plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: Metal Oxide Catalyzed Epitaxy (MOCATAXY) of (010) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> was investigated using In as a catalyst in plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Expansion of the (010) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> growth regime to higher growth temperatures and Ga fluxes was demonstrated. A maximum growth rate of 5 nm/min was achieved, doubling that of conventional growth. Smooth surface morphology of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.6\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> film with root mean squared roughness of 0.12 nm was shown. Sn doping of MOCATAXY (010) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> was demonstrated up to concentrations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\ \mathrm{x}\ 10^{18}\ \mathrm{cm} ^{-3}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Suppressing Interdiffusion of Si in Er-doped CeO2/ Si(111) and Its Impact on the Optical Property
abstract: We have investigated the crystallinity and optical properties of the Er-doped CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (Er:CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) layers grown on the Si substrates. We paid attention to the interdiffusion of Si, which degrades optical properties of the Er:CeO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers. To avoid the interdiffusion, it turned out that lower growth temperature and/or insertion of the CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> buffer layer are/is effective. When the growth temperature is ≤700°C, the 20-nm-thick CeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> buffer layer is enough to avoid the Si-Er complexes formation, with which the sharp and intense PL emission is achieved.

articleTitle: Quasi-ballistic thermal phonon transport in nanostructured Si nanowires
abstract: We demonstrate directional heat flux in silicon nanowires based on quasi-ballistic phonon transport property within phonon mean free path. A corrugated nanowire formed directionality of the thermal phonons and results in directional heat flux. This effect makes guiding and even focusing of heat fluxes in a certain spatial position in silicon membranes. We demonstrate routing of thermal phonons using a directional heat flux generator formed by a corrugated structure. Crossover of quasi-ballistic to diffusive phonon transport is also demonstrated by comparing a straight and serpentine nanowire structures. The series of experiments demonstrate highly advanced thermal management in semiconductors and open new possibility in the thermal engineering field.

articleTitle: Integrated synthesis of graphene nanoribbon-based field effect transistor with high on/off ratio
abstract: Graphene nanoribbon (GNR)-based field effect transistor (FET) with high on/off current ratio has been fabricated with direct conversion of nanobar catalyst under plasma CVD. Ge nanobar catalyst can obtain relatively narrow width of GNR, resulting in the high on/off ratio of GNR-based FET. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements reveal that locally formed fine structures in GNR can be the origin of high on/off. Since this method possesses significant scalability for integrated synthesis of GNR, it can be a promising method for the practical application of GNR, especially in semiconductor device field.

articleTitle: Development of High-power High-thermal Conductivity GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors
abstract: We demonstrate a silicon via backend process for AlGaN/GaN-on-Si (111) platform-based devices which was processed by assisted back grinding, chemical mechanical polishing, deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) and copper (Cu) electroplating. The DC output characteristics can be improved about 20% after the introduction of backside via and copper heat dissipation layer. Moreover, the improvement also can be seen from the load-pull measurements under 20%, 25% and 30% duty cycle. Under higher pulse width operation, the more obvious improvement of output current can be observed. These results indicate that the substrate removal and copper filling technique are effective to achieve high-performance AlGaN/GaN HEMTs.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of III-V/Si Hybrid MOS Microdisk Modulator
abstract: An optical modulator consisting of microdisk resonator with a III-V/Si hybrid MOS capacitor is numerical analyzed. A III-V mesa bonded on a Si slab enables a microdisk resonator with a radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, resulting in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\pi}\mathrm{L}$</tex> of 0.032 Vcm. The proposed modulator is suitable for ultrasmall, efficient optical modulators.

articleTitle: Development of Hall Effect Sensor on AlGaN/GaN FinFET Structure
abstract: In order to improve the sensitivity of the embedded Hall-effect sensor in AlGaN/GaN integrated circuit and achieve a high-temperature high-sensitivity sensor performance, the analyses for optimized Fin structure for the GaN Hall-effect device are presented in this paper. In the process, the influences of the relaxation degree and the current density on the Hall voltage are both considered to obtain the best design. Both the calculated and the 3-D simulation results are obtained. It is shown that the sensitivity is strongly dependent on the width of the fin dimension.

articleTitle: Enabling Low Temperature Aluminum Nitride ALD by Use of a Novel Hydrazine Source
abstract: Aluminum nitride (AlN) ALD has attracted recent attention because it is a direct wide-bandgap, III-V semiconductor with excellent dielectric and piezoelectric properties, good thermal conductivity, and high mechanical strength. There is a need for low temperature ALD to prevent the detrimental effects of atomic diffusion. However, thermal ALD of AlN with NH3/Trimethyl Aluminum (TMA) precursors is problematic below 450°C.

articleTitle: Fabrication of CH3NH3PbBr3 Based Perovskite Single Crystal Arrays by Spin-coating Method Using Hydrophobic Patterned Substrate
abstract: Simple and low-cost fabrication technique of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> based perovskite single crystal arrays via combination of spin-coating and hydrophobic patterned substrate are proposed. By optimizing the substrate surface treatment, blending ratio of precursor solution, and spinning condition, the precursor solution was uniformly aligned on hydrophobic pattern area and perovskite single crystals are precipitated at the center of the pattern area. By changing the halogen composition of precursor solution, the emission color was varied from blue (447 nm) to red (742 nm). The structural and optical characteristics of precipitated perovskites crystals will be reported.

articleTitle: Control of absorption properties of MEMS terahertz bolometers using metamaterials
abstract: We have investigated terahertz (THz) metamaterial absorbers to achieve narrowband absorption properties for microelectromechanical (MEMS) THz bolometers in order to have better matching with the illumination by quantum cascade lasers in THz imaging applications. We have found that metal-insulator-metal (MIM) sandwich structure is crucial to achieve a large THz absorption. The absorption depends on the thickness (h) of the insulator layer. The maximum absorption reached 88% at around 3 THz when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{h}=1400\ \text{nm}$</tex>. The observed absorption spectrum was in good agreement with theory.

articleTitle: Dimension Engineering of Narrow Bandgap Semiconductor InAs Nanostructures in Wafer-Scale
abstract: We demonstrate an approach that provides a precise control of the dimension of InAs from one-dimensional (1-D) nanowires to wafer-scale free-standing two-dimensional (2-D) nanosheets, which have a high degree of crystallinity, using molecular-beam epitaxy by controlling catalyst alloy segregation. In our approach, 2-D InAs nanosheets can be obtained directly from 1-D InAs nanowires by silver-indium alloy segregation, which is much easier than all previously reported method, such as traditional buffering technique and select area epitaxial growth. Detailed transmission electron microscopy investigations provide a solid evidence that the catalyst alloy segregation is the origination of the InAs dimensional transformation from 1-D nanowires to 2-D nanosheets, and even to three-dimensional complex crosses. Using this method, we find that the wafer-scale free-standing InAs nanosheets can be grown on various substrates including Si, MgO, sapphire and GaAs etc. The InAs nanosheets grown at high temperature are pure phase single crystals. Our work will open up a conceptually new and general technology route toward the effective controlling the dimension of the low-dimensional III-V semiconductors. It may also enable the low-cost fabrication of free-standing nanosheet-based devices on an industrial scale.

articleTitle: Liquid Crystals as Polycrystalline Materials for Organic Thin Film Transistors
abstract: I show the benefits of liquid crystallinity in soluble crystalline organic thin film transistor (OTFT) materials. Liquid crystallinity helps us to control molecular alignments and fabricate uniform crystalline films by solution process. Our developed OTFT material, phenyl-benzothienobenzothiophene derivative, Ph-BTBT-10, shows good transistor performance after thermal annealing. Furthermore, the variation of transistor performance is quite small, and the standard deviation divided by average is less than 10%. I conclude that the best use of liquid crystallinity in OTFT materials is the key for practical applications of OTFTs.

articleTitle: Elimination of photothermal effect on nano-mechanical resonator consisting of optically transparent h-BN sheet
abstract: Two-dimensional atomic layer materials with optically transparent materials such as h-BN are expected to be high performance nano-electro-mechanical resonators (NEMR). Elimination of the photothermal effect is very crucial for accurate force sensing using NEMR. Thus, the optically transparent material such as h-BN is one of strong candidates for this purpose. Here, we investigate the photothermal effect on the mechanical resonance properties of the h-BN-NEMR driven by electrostatically using the dielectric effect.

articleTitle: Study on epitaxial lift-off of stacked GaAs solar cells for low-cost photovoltaic application
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for the cost reduction of III-V solar cells. A two-layer stacked GaAs solar cell was grown on a GaAs substrate by solid-source molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). Al(Ga)As release layers were inserted between each GaAs cells and substrate. After the growth, we separated the staked cell structures into two single cells using epitaxial lift-off (ELO) with HF solution, which selectively etches Al(Ga)As layer. Thin film GaAs cells were transferred to flexible carriers. For an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\omega-2\theta$</tex> scan around the high-resolution x-ray diffraction (HRXRD) (004) measurement, a strong peak caused by GaAs layer were observed for both thin GaAs solar cells. This result suggests that high crystal quality was maintained for both thin film GaAs cells even after ELO process and proves to possible to separate stacked cell structures into individual layers. We are studying the fast fabrication of III-V solar cells using hydride vapor phase eptitaxy (HVPE), which can deposit layers at growth rate of around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\ \mu \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{h}$</tex>. If multi-layer ELO technique is applicable to multiple-stacked solar cell structures grown by HVPE, it is possible to decrease significantly the cost of III-V solar cells.

articleTitle: Ultraflexible Biosignal Amplifier Based on Organic Thin-Film Transistors
abstract: In this study, we have developed an ultraflexible and bio-conformable organic voltage amplifier circuits. The organic circuits were fabricated on an ultraflexible <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> -thick parylene foil with p-channel OTFTs and thin-film capacitors, and therefore, showing highly mechanical flexibility to attach onto a soft human skin surface. Here, we will introduce two types of voltage amplifier circuits. One is a pseudo-CMOS inverter based single-end amplifier, which shows signal gain over 60 dB. And the other is a differential amplification circuit, which has a capability of amplifying differential input signal while suppressing common-mode noise. To demonstrate the potential of improving signal integrity for biosignal monitoring, we have recorded human electroencephalogram (EEG) or electrocardiogram (ECG) signal. As a result, the small EEG signal in the micro-volt range can be amplified to mV level. In other case, using the differential amplifier, the environmental artifacts such as 60 Hz electrical harmonic noise and human motion artifacts of the input signal was suppressed by approximately 20 times, yielding ECG signals with an improved signal-to-noise-ratio of 21.7 dB.

articleTitle: Impact of the insertion of AlGaN back barrier on crystal quality, $\boldsymbol{N}_{\mathbf{S}}$, and mobility of GaN-channel HEMTs with high-Al-content AlGaN top barrier grown on high-resistivity Si substrate
abstract: We investigate the impact of inserting an AlGaN back barrier on the crystal quality and electrical characteristics of GaN-channel HEMTs with a thin AlGaN top barrier grown on high-resistivity Si substrate. AFM and XRD measurements revealed that the AlGaN back barrier does not significantly affect the crystal quality of the HEMT layers. However, the channel electron mobility decreases as the thickness of the GaN channel (an AlGaN back barrier) decreases (increases), which is probably due to interface roughness and alloy scattering. For further enhancement of the high-frequency characteristics of scaled GaN-channel HEMTs on Si, it is important to consider these influences of AlGaN back barrier insertion in designing HEMT layer structures.

articleTitle: Graphene Stabilized Two-Dimensional Crystals
abstract: The spectrum of two-dimensional (2D) and layered materials “beyond graphene” has been continually expanding. The realization of wide bandgap 2D materials “beyond hexagonal boron nitride (hBN)”, however, has been limited. Group-III nitride semiconductors such as indium nitride (InN), gallium nitride (GaN), and aluminum nitride (AlN) are proposed to have thickness tunable energy bandgaps ranging from 0.7 – 7.0 eV as a result of quantum confinement. Despite the extensive computational discovery of 2D materials, the synthesis of 2D III-nitrides “beyond hBN” is still elusive. We demonstrate for the first time that 2D atomic layers of GaN not only can be stabilized, but also exhibit unique structural properties from that of bulk material.

articleTitle: In situ synchrotron X-ray reciprocal space mapping during InGaN/GaN heterostructure nanowire growth
abstract: In situ synchrotron X-ray reciprocal space mapping was carried out to investigate the evolution of lattice strain and crystal structure of InGaN/GaN heterostructure nanowires grown by molecular beam epitaxy. At the beginning of the growth, the InGaN lattice was compressively strained to that of GaN, resulting in the pseudomorphic growth. This strain started to relax at a thickness of 3 nm and fully relaxed at 9 nm. Concomitantly, polytypes consisting of the zinc-blende and wurtzite phases were formed in InGaN.

articleTitle: Dislocation free InP/lnGaAs/lnP islands on Si by micro-channel selective area MOVPE
abstract: III-V monolithic integration on Si have long been the key component in silicon photonics toward inter/intra chip interconnections. Besides, efficient and low-cost integration of III-V on Si provides unique and attractive solutions for application such as bio-sensing, HEMT, IR imaging, and eye-safe LIDAR. To this end, selective area growth (SAG) of InP and related materials on Si(111) have been widely explored. However, due to the limitations in geometry and growth scheme, large area of material and high crystal quality cannot be both achieved.

articleTitle: Transmission Characteristics of a Novel Waveguide Structure for Wavelength Division Multiplexing
abstract: We investigate a novel photonic crystal (PhC) waveguide structure, which consists of a displaced row of air holes in the hexagonal PhC. We found that the large bandwidth of the waveguide is favorable for waveguide division multiplexing which is promising for high-capacity data transfer. In addition, three-dimensional finite-differential time-domain (FDTD) calculations have revealed that light loss in this waveguide is smaller than that in the conventional W1 waveguide.

articleTitle: Room-Temperature Electrically Pumped InP-based $1.3\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$ Quantum Dot Laser on on-axis (001) Silicon
abstract: We report the first InAlGaAs/InP 1.3um quantum dots (QDs) laser grown on (001) silicon by MOCVD. Optimized QDs growth allows lasing on V-grooved and planar silicon templates. The threshold current density of the laser on V-grooved silicon is around 1.0 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Effect of introducing optical blanking to GaN epitaxy by using pulsed laser deposition technology
abstract: We found that blanking-mode operation of Pico-second Laser Epitaxy enables dramatic reduction of the sheet resistance with good uniformity for the epitaxial growth of Ge-doped GaN layer. Attained carrier density exceeds over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.5\times 10^{20}\text{cm}^{-3}$</tex>, which is good enough to achieve non-alloy ohmic contact regardless of the overlaying metal. Duty cycle for the pulse-mode operation can be simply controlled by rotating half-wave plate outside the vacuum chamber. By using the blanking-mode, we achieved complete elimination of the Ga droplet even at the growth temperature below 500 °C. The proposed blanking mechanism can be easily introduced by the simple optical system without using mechanical shutter, thus we believe the present technique is a useful technique for industrializing PLD technology.

articleTitle: First-principles study of defect properties in radiation-detectable TlBr
abstract: Thallium bromide (T1Br) is a promisingsemiconductor for the fabrication of radiation detectors because of its large carrier mobilityand high gamma-ray stopping power.

articleTitle: Effects of Ga-OH Bond at Initial GaN Surface on Electrical Characteristics of SiO2/GaN Interface
abstract: Effects of Ga-OH bond at the GaN surface on the electrical characteristics of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/GaN MOS capacitor were investigated. Three surface treatments (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> anneal, UV/ozone and HPWVA) were utilized to change the ratio of Ga-OH at the GaN surface. It was found that fixed charge (Qf) before PMA showed a tendency to decrease with increasing the ratio of Ga-OH bond at initial surface. It is considered that the -OH bond on the GaN surface needs to be reduced due to formation of the fixed charges and the charge traps. On the other hand, after PMA, Qf values of each sample were almost the same regardless of the initial surface states of each treatment.

articleTitle: Effects of Impurity Hubbard Bands on the Hall Effect in n-InP
abstract: The low-temperature data of Hall-effect measurements on n-type InP samples have been analyzed on the basis of an impurity-Hubbard-band model with taking into account the temperature dependence of the Hall factor for hopping conduction in impurity Hubbard bands. As for the hopping conduction mechanism, we assumed nearest-neighbor hopping (NNH) in the top Hubbard band (D- band) while assumed variable-range hopping (VRH) in the bottom Hubbard band (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{D}^{0}$</tex> band). The activation energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{2}$</tex> for NNH conduction in the D- band has been deduced and is shown to obey the relation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{2}\propto(\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{ND}}-\mathrm{d}_{0\mathrm{cr}})^{1/3}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{ND}}$</tex> is the average net donor separation, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}_{0\mathrm{cr}}$</tex> is its critical value at which the metal-insulator transition occurs, and K is the compensation ratio. The Hall coefficient as well as the Hall mobility in the temperature range of 8–25 K, in which the Hall coefficient has its maximum, is shown to be dominated by the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{2}$</tex> conduction in the D- band. The characteristic temperature of the Mott VRH in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{D}^{0}$</tex> band has been deduced and is shown to be decrease with the donor concentration.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Boron Nitride Nanophotonics
abstract: Hexagonal Boron Nitride (hBN) mono and multilayers are promising hosts for room temperature single photon emitters (SPEs) with excellent optical properties. In this work, we use high energy (~MeV) electron irradiation as a means to generate stable SPEs in hBN. Four different types of exfoliated hBN flakes were subjected to the study- namely, high purity multilayers, isotopically pure hBN, carbon rich hBN multilayers and monolayered material. The results indicate that electron irradiation increases emitter concentrations dramatically in all samples. Furthermore, the engineered emitters are distributed on all over the flat areas of the flakes, and that makes it easy to integrate hBN into photonic devices. After electron expose, the fluorescent emitters do not require activation by high temperature annealing of the host material. Our results provide important insights into controlled formation of hBN SPEs and may aid in identification of their crystallographic origin.

articleTitle: Selective-area MOVPE growth of multi-$\lambda$ InGaAlAs-based MQWs on patterned InP-on-insulator substrate
abstract: We demonstrate the selective-area metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) growth of InGaAlAs MQWs on an InP membrane directly bonded to a SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Si substrate (InP-on-insulator substrate). We obtained MQWs with multiple wavelengths ranging from 1204 to 1276 nm in a single growth by changing the design of the selective-area growth mask formed on the InP membrane. The PL wavelengths for the MQWs grown with different masks range from 1204 to 1276 nm with no obvious degradation, which shows the potential for fabricating multi-lambda laser arrays and EADFB lasers. We also demonstrate the fabrication of buried-heterostructures by the regrowth of InP. Both the wafer-level and longitudinal-direction uniformity of the active region are very high.

articleTitle: Observation on Carrier Dynamics of Intermediate Band in Multi Stacked InGaAs Quantum Dots using Two Color Excitation
abstract: We investigated the intermediate formation band and the electronic structures in multi-stacked QDs with different inter dot spacing using theory and experimental techniques: photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy with 2-color excitation. We observed different behaviors with respect to inter dot spacing of 15nm and 7nm. These results offer an existence of the intermediate band formation and carrier dynamics in the multi stacked QDs.

articleTitle: Thin-Film Transistors Based on Copper Phthalocyanine Deposited on a Gate Dielectric Rubbed with Poly(tetrafluoroethylene)
abstract: Copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) thin-film transistors (TFTs) having a SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate dielectric rubbed with poly(tetrafluoroethylene) (PTFE) have been fabricated to investigate the influence of the rubbing on the TFT performance. An atomic microscope image of the substrate rubbed with PTFE revealed the presence of alignment layer formed on the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface. For the surface of the substrate with the alignment layer, a water droplet for water contact measurement exhibited anisotropy. Furthermore, the field-effect mobilities of CuPc TFTs depended on the the angle between the rubbing direction and the conduction direction of the channel carrier. The mobility for 0° has the highest value in the TFTs with a PTFE alignment layer. The difference between the mobilities of TFTs for 0° and without an alignment layer is not clear because of the large variation in the mobility of TFT for 0°. The variation of the alignment layer may cause the variation in the mobility. However, two TFTs for 0° had high mobilities as compared to those of TFTs without an alignment layer. This result suggests that improvement in reproducibility of a PTFE alignment layer enhance the mobility of TFTs with the alignment layer.

articleTitle: Control of electron spin at spin-resolved quantum Hall edges
abstract: Magnetic field and spin-orbit interaction (SOI) are representative freedoms that can be entangled to electron spins. In experiments, while magnetic field strong enough for the control of spin is difficult to be localized onto the area for single spins such as quantum dots, the orbit can be localized to narrow regions with mesoscopic structures. Hence for quantum information manipulation borne by electron spins, the control through SOI has an advantage in that sense.

articleTitle: InxGa1-xN Alloys Grown by Plasma-Assisted Molecular Beam Epitaxy (PAMBE) with Growth Rates Up to $1.3\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}/\mathbf{hr}$
abstract: In this work In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>N films were grown with growth rates up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.30\ \mu \mathrm{m}/\text{hr}$</tex> enabled by large active nitrogen fluxes up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.5\ \mu \mathrm{m}/\text{hr}$</tex> while maintaining high quality crystal structure and surface morphology. At growth temperatures of 550 and 600°C compositions up to In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.22</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.78</inf>N were achieved. Minor In incorporation was observed at 700°C, and further optimization of growth parameters is expected to yield moderate In incorporation at this temperature.

articleTitle: Investigation of InAs Quantum Dot Deformation During Capping with an InGaAs Layer Using Time-resolved RHEED Measurements
abstract: We report the characterization of InAs quantum dots (QDs) capped with an InGaAs layer using the time-resolved reflection high energy electron diffraction (RHEED) intensity measurements. The decay rate of the RHEED intensity from the InAs QDs during the capping process reduced with an increase in In composition in the capping layer. The RHEED intensity decay rate, which was determined by the inflection point of differentiated fitting curves of RHEED intensity, can be related with the deformation of the QDs owing to the diffusion of In atoms during the capping process. In addition, cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy observations of the buried QDs revealed that the mean height of the QDs capped with an In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>As layer was larger than that of QDs capped with a GaAs layer. These results suggest that a capping layer with high In composition suppresses the deformation of QDs and results in a red-shift of emission wavelength of the buried QDs.

articleTitle: Impurity and isotope control of cubic and hexagonal boron nitride crystals under solution growth process
abstract: Some progresses in the synthesis of high purity hexagonal boron nitride BN (hBN) crystals were achieved by using Ba-BN as a growth solvent material at high pressure. The key issue to obtain high purity crystals is to reduce oxygen and carbon contamination in the growth circumstances. It is emphasized that hBN crystals exhibits superior properties as ultra violet light emitter as well as a substrate of graphene devices. While the current subject is to realize how the major impurities such as carbon and oxygen affect the properties of hBN and cBN, some progerss for the realization for the application of 2D's substrates and photonic materials have been achieved.

articleTitle: Demonstration of InAs nanowire vertical transistors
abstract: This paper reports on selective-area growth of vertical InAs/InAsP core-shell (CS) NWs on Si, and demonstration of vertical surrounding-gate transistors (SGTs) and InAs/InP CS NW-Si heterojunction TFET. NWs were grown by selective-area metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy (SA-MOVPE). The growth temperature was 550°C and III/V ratio was 256. Zn-pulsed doping layer was grown for 5 min, followed by Si-doped InAs growth for 3 min and growth of Sn-pulsed-doped layer for 5 min. Finally, InP shell was grown for 7 sec. As for InAsP layer, the P content in vapor phase was 40%. The SGT exhibits minimum subthreshold slope (SS) of 88 mV/decade at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{DS}}=0.50\ \mathrm{V}$</tex> and low leakage current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 10^{-12} \mathrm{A}/\mu \mathrm{m})$</tex>. ON-state current for the CS NW-channel was 2 times higher than bare InAs NW SGTs. This was assumed that the elastic strain due to lattice mismatch in CS layer was supperss electron scattering process. The TFET showed SS of 46 mV/decade which was below physical limitation of FET (60 mV/decade). The on/off ratio of 2 decade at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{DS}}=0.50\ \mathrm{V}$</tex> due to low source doping level. Further design of source region and shell structure will be discussed to enhance ON-state current.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Germanium Doping to GaP-based Dilute Nitrides
abstract: Dilute III-V nitride alloys such as GaPN and GaAsPN are essential candidates of materials for light emitting or light absorbing devices on Si substrates due to their perfect lattice matching to Si. For device applications, impurity doping and the concentration control are important issues. However, with the conventional dopants such as Si, Te and S, carrier concentration drastically decreased with N composition increased. This paper presents intentional doping of germanium (Ge) to GaP-based III-V-N alloys by using molecular beam epitaxy. The carrier concentration of Ge-doped GaAsPN was increased with N composition in contrast to conventional dopants such as S and Si. From temperature characteristics of Hall effect measurement, it is revealed that activation energy is decreased with N composition, while Ge concentration in the alloy is constant value. In addition, we found that background doping level of Ge is extremely low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(< 10^{15}\mathrm{cm}^{-3})$</tex> compared to S. As a result, Ge is a promising candidate as a new dopant for III-V-N alloys.

articleTitle: GaN-based Inverter by Monolithic Integration of Threshold Controlled MOSFETs
abstract: Fabrication and device characteristics of GaN-based inverter is investigated towards future GaN-based functional monolithic integrated circuit. n-channel enhancement and depletion mode MOSFETs (E-MOSFET and D-MOSFET) were fabricated on a low-density Mg-doped p-GaN substrate. Threshold voltage control of MOS-FET to obtain D-MOSFET was made by preferential Si implantation. Operation of E-MOSFET and D-MOSFET was confirmed in I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</inf> and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> characteristics. Successful operation of E/D type inverter with a maximum voltage gain beyond unity was demonstrated in monolithically integrated E-MOSFET and D-MOSFET on a same chip.

articleTitle: Atomically-Thin Photovoltaics: Progress, Promise and Interface Physics
abstract: We report innovative methods for trapping nearly 100% light over a broadband portion of visible spectrum into sub-15 nm thickness transition metal dichalcogenide semiconductors. We further show that these strongly absorbing ultrathin heterostructures can be converted into high external quantum efficiency photovoltaic (PV) cells and finally also present a way to engineer band alignment and high open circuit voltage in < 15 nm thick PVs. I will conclude with future perspective and outlook on atomically thin photovoltaics.

articleTitle: Smart Stack Technology for III-V/Si Multi-Junction Solar Cells
abstract: Developing a handy strategy towards III-V/Si integration has been a longstanding challenge in the photovoltaic community, and its demand is rapidly increasing to prepare for the future demand of higher-efficiency solar cells. To this end, we have proposed “smart stack” technology, an approach using metal nanoparticle arrays to interconnect III-V and Si both electrically and optically. This presentation overviews the concept, process, and device demonstration of this technology, including some of the recent progress.

articleTitle: Physical vapor transport growth of trigonal selenium crystal
abstract: Unique anisotropic crystal structure has received much attention as showing superior electronic, magnetic and thermoelectric properties. Recently, trigonal selenium (t-Se) and tellurium (t-Te) have been studied as one-dimensional semiconductor materials. The crystal structures consist of helically arranged atomic chains along the c-axis direction, which are coupled individually by weak van der Waals interactions to form a hexagonal lattice structure. We investigated the growth of trigonal selenium (t-Se) films by physical vapor transport. X-ray diffraction (XRD) peak of the t-Se were detected. From Raman spectroscopy, analysis three active vibration photon modes originated from t-Se are clearly observed. The t-Se could be confirmed by analyzing the XRD patterns and Raman spectra.

articleTitle: In situ study of strain and composition of InGaN/GaN multi-quantum-well nanowires
abstract: The molecular beam epitaxial (MBE) growth of twenty-period InGaN/GaN multi-quantum-well (MQW) nanowires was investigated by in situ X-ray reciprocal space mapping (in situ RSM). The evolution of strain, composition, and their inhomogeneities during the growth significantly varied with increasing number of QWs. After the growth of the ninth QWs, InGaN was tensilely strained with poor crystalline quality as inferred from the diffraction peak position and shape. At the same time, another peak emerged at the higher indium composition, suggesting the segregation of InN in the MQW nanowires.

articleTitle: Chemical vapor deposition growth of boron incorporated graphitic carbon nitride film for carbon based semiconductor systems
abstract: For the creation of carbon based semiconductor systems, we have proposed controlling the bandgap energy toward the blue/ultraviolet or red/infrared region by incorporating substitutional atoms into graphitic carbon nitride (g-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) as novel synthesis method to realize the Hexagonal boron carbon nitride (h-BCN). B incorporated g-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> films were grown by thermal chemical vapor deposition using melamine and ammonia borane as source species. B incorporation into g-C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, which was indicated the substitution for C atoms, could be confirmed by analyzing the individual atomic bonds and stoichiometric chemical composition. Photoluminescence spectra exhibited the peak shift toward to high energy side, expecting the impact of B incorporation on energy band structure.

articleTitle: One-dimensional electronic states in highly-stacked InAs/GaAs quantum dot superlattices
abstract: We have studied one-dimensional (1D) electronic states of highly-stacked InAs/GaAs quantum dot superlattices by time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) measurements. The PL decay profile measured at low temperature exhibited a combination of a single exponential decay and a stretched exponential decay due to the recombination of the carriers spatially separated in the ES miniband, which indicates the 1D miniband formation only in the ES. As the measurement temperature was raised, the decay lifetime of the fast decay component gradually increased and obeyed the T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> dependence due to the 1D translational motion of excitons in the FS. Therefore, the 1D miniband formation was confirmed in the FS as well as in the ES.

articleTitle: Equivalent oxide thickness scaling for efficient III-V/Si hybrid MOS optical phase shifter
abstract: III-V/Si hybrid metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) optical phase shifter, which is enabled by the wafer bonding technology, allows for efficient, low-power and low-loss optical phase control. Reducing the equivalent oxide thickness is effective to enhance its modulation efficiency. In this study, we demonstrated the capacitance equivalent thickness scaling down to 3.5 nm by employing HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> stack for wafer bonding, which is expected to results in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\pi}\mathrm{L}$</tex> around 0.035 Vcm.

articleTitle: The Josephson effect in InAs quantum wells with the spin Hall effect
abstract: The Josephson supercurrent in ballistic superconductor/normal metal/superconductor (SNS) junctions is carried through the Andreev bound states (ABS) formed in the normal conductor. These virtual states of traversing electrons and holes are modulated but not destroyed by time-reversal symmetry conserving perturbation. However, we found that the critical current of the Nb/InAs/Nb junctions are strongly suppressed by the spin current, which keeps time-reversal symmetry.

articleTitle: Large area hexagonal boron nitride coatings for SERS applications with silver nanoparticles
abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a two-dimensional, wide-bandgap semiconductor which has a honeycomb like structure similar to that of graphene. hBN sheets has been shown to be highly effective in protecting metals against oxidation at high temperatures.

articleTitle: Wafer-scale single-crystal hexagonal boron nitride film via self-collimated grain formation
abstract: Although polycrystalline hexagonal boron nitride (PC-hBN) has been realized, defects and grain boundaries still cause charge scatterings and trap sites, impeding high-performance electronics. Here, we report a method of synthesizing wafer-scale single-crystalline hBN (SC-hBN) monolayer films by chemical vapor deposition. The limited solubility of boron (B) and nitrogen (N) atoms in liquid gold promotes high diffusion of adatoms on the surface of liquid at high temperature to provoke the circular hBN grains. These further evolve into closely packed unimodal grains by means of self-collimation of B and N edges inherited by electrostatic interaction between grains, eventually forming an SC-hBN film on a wafer scale. This SC-hBN film also allows for the synthesis of wafer-scale graphene/hBN heterostructure and single-crystalline tungsten disulfide.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Acoustic Dynamics in Nanoelectromechanical Waveguides
abstract: Nonlinearity is the key to control a traveling wave beyond linear regime. In contrast to a field of optics where highly functional devices have been developed utilizing the optical nonlinearity, making use of nonlinear effect in a field of acoustic devices has yet to be fully performed. This is due to the lack of a suitable platform realizing a low-loss waveguide as well as an efficient electro-acoustic transduction enough to excite and propagate an intense nonlinear acoustic wave. In this study, we have demonstrated that most fundamental nonlinear phenomena of self-phase modulation and four-wave mixing are fully realized using a developed platform of nanoelectrome-chanical waveguides. Combining the leading-edge technology of high-crystalline-quality nanoelectromechanical waveguide with piezoelectric interdigital transducer, we efficiently excite an intense and long-lived traveling wave enough to induce and characterize acoustic nonlinearity. The observed nonlinear phenomena are perfectly described by the model using the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, so that this system enables the nonlinear dynamics to be precisely tuned. The design flexibility and integratability of this platform extend the ability to manipulate acoustic wave propagation on a chip, thus holding promise for promoting highly-functional acoustic devices and investigating nonlinear acoustics.

articleTitle: Mid-infrared photoresponse and robotic fabrication of graphene/h-BN van der Waals heterostructures
abstract: We present our recent experiments on mid-infrared photoresponse due to cyclotron resonance absorption in van der Waals junctions of graphene and 2D materials; (i) photo-thermoelectric effect in graphene /h-BN, (ii) photon-assisted thermionic emission in graphene/MoS2, (iii) electrical control of cyclotron resonance frequency in trilayer graphene/h-BN. We also present autonomous robotic searching and van der Waals assembly of 2D materials.

articleTitle: Ballistic spin locking in a two-dimensional Rashba system
abstract: Coherent spin rotation is a prerequisite for processing spin information in spintronics and for acquiring quantum information. The spin state is typically controlled by applying an external magnetic field to induce spin precessional motion around the field axis. While electrical spin control is possible using the effective magnetic field induced by the spin-orbit (SO) interaction, the functionality of spin manipulation is still based on rotation around this field. Here we report a new concept of spin manipulation by controlling electron orbital motion at the nanoscale: electron spin rotates in a circular orbital motion while spin orientation is locked towards the SO field rather than the spin precession. This effect, which we have termed “ballistic spin locking”, illustrates the interconnectivity of the electron spin and orbital motion in a ballistic regime and allows us to extend control of the spin states beyond the limits imposed by rotation around the magnetic field.

articleTitle: 1-aminopyrene-modified epitaxial graphene device for pH sensors
abstract: 1-aminopyrene-modified epitaxial graphene devices were fabricated to realize epitaxial graphene based pH sensors because the epitaxial graphene film synthesized on the SiC substrate is intrinsically insensitive for ions owing to the single crystal and very few surface defects. The transport characteristics shifted in the positive gate voltage direction with increasing pH while no shift was observed in the bare epitaxial graphene device. It can be considered that functionalized epitaxial graphene film have high potential for the various chemical and biological sensors.

articleTitle: All solid-state 2D tunnel FET
abstract: 2D materials are highly promising for tunnel FETs with low subthreshold swing and high drive current because the shorter tunnel distance and strong gate controllability can be expected from the van der Waals gap distance and the atomically sharp heterointerface formed independently of lattice matching. However, the common problem for 2D-2D TFETs is the lack of highly doped 2D materials with the high process stability as the sources. In this study, we have found that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p^{+}$</tex>-WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> doped by charge transfer from a WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> surface oxide layer can be stabilized by transferring it onto a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$h$</tex>-BN substrate. Using this <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p^{+}$</tex>-WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as a source, we fabricate all-solid-state 2D-2D heterostructure TFETs with an Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> top gate insulator, i.e., type-III <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p^{+}$</tex>-WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/WSe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The band-to-band tunneling and negative differential resistance trends are clearly demonstrated at low temperatures. This work suggests that high doped 2D crystal of the charge transfer type is an excellent choice as sources for TFETs.

articleTitle: Investigation of Fe incorporation in (010) $\beta$-Ga2O3 films grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: The incorporation of Fe into (010) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> films grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy was investigated. Fe was found to incorporate heavily into films grown at 500 °C while growth temperatures of 650 °C and higher showed a significantly longer tail of Fe into the films. This Fe tail was determined to be a result of surface riding during growth rather than diffusion. The total surface riding concentration of Fe was found to be about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\ \mathrm{x} 10^{12}\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$</tex> from typical Fe doped (010) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrates. Surface segregation coefficients of 0.9819 and 0.9901 were calculated for growth temperatures of 500 °C and 700 °C respectively.

articleTitle: Vapor-Solid Selective Area Molecular Beam Epitaxy and N-Type Doping of Catalyst-Free GaAs:Si Nanowires on Silicon
abstract: In vapor-liquid-solid GaAs NWs, doping control has proven to be difficult due to non-uniform incorporation and strong amphoteric behavior of Si dopants in the presence of a liquid droplet catalyst. We present for the first time clear evidence of n-type doping in direct bottom-up growth of GaAs:Si NWs by catalyst-free selective area molecular beam epitaxy.

articleTitle: Spin Blockade and Magnetoresistance in Double Quantum Well Diode with Inverted Electric Field
abstract: In the last century the band-gap engineering including modulation doping technique, largely expanded the possibility of solid state devices. The concept of topology came into our view in the beginning of the present century. The first claim of topological insulator utilized quantum well to kill the topological anomaly in HgTe. Synthesis of artificial topological material is then one of the next target.

articleTitle: Quantum entangled photon emitting diodes based on GaAs quantum dots on (111)A: Robustness against increasing temperature
abstract: Recently, we have realized highly symmetric GaAs quantum dots (QD)/AlGaAs on GaAs (111)A surface by droplet epitaxy, and confirmed the generation of quantum entangled photon pairs. In those studies, we used a short-pulsed laser for optical excitation. For practical applications, however, development of an electrically driven device is essential. In this study, we report the generation of quantum entangled photon pairs by current injection and their temperature dependence.

articleTitle: Radiative and Nonradiative Tunneling in Nanowire Light-Emitting Diodes
abstract: We investigated the temperature dependence of the I-V and emission properties of InP nanowire light-emitting diodes (LEDs) grown by selective-area metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy in detail to elucidate their carrier injection and recombination mechanisms. Very weak temperature dependence of the I-V characteristics revealed that carrier transport occurred with tunneling through the pn junction. In addition, our observation in the bias-voltage dependence of electroluminescence (EL) peak position and intensity, and photon energy dependence of the low-energy tail of EL peaks at low temperature indicated the radiative tunneling. A discrepancy of the tunneling factor between I-V characteristics and EL was found, suggesting the existence of a large nonradiative component in the tunneling current.

articleTitle: Investigation of second harmonic generation efficiency in ultrahigh-Q SiC photonic crystal nanocavities
abstract: In this work, we experimentally investigate the characteristics of second harmonic generation (SHG) in SiC photonic crystal nanocavities with ultrahigh-Q factors of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>. The powers of fundamental input light and SHG output are precisely measured, and the normalized SHG efficiency is evaluated. A high SHG efficiency of the order of 1000%/W is obtained in a SiC photonic crystal nanocavity with a Q factor of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Avalanche Noise in GaN PN Junctions Grown on Native GaN Substrates
abstract: GaN pn junction diodes grown on native GaN substrates have been fabricated and characterized. The temperature-dependent current-voltage characteristics exhibit a positive temperature coefficient of breakdown as expected from impact ionization avalanche. However, for IMPATT and avalanche photodiode applications, device noise is very important. The low frequency noise characteristics of these devices have been measured under forward and reverse bias conditions. The forward noise spectra is dominated by 1/f noise, and the current spectral density is proportional to I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.6</sup>. Under reverse bias, the noise spectra show 1/f noise at reverse biases below the avalanche threshold. However, at reverse biases in the avalanche regime, the multiplication noise overwhelms the 1/f noise, resulting in a white noise spectrum. The measured results are consistent with expectations from avalanche noise theory.

articleTitle: Adsorbtion of Oxygen and Hydrogen Atoms on the GaAs(110) Surface
abstract: We report scanning tunneling microscope (STM) investigations of oxygen and hydrogen adsorbation on the GaAs(110) surface in comparison with the clean GaAs(110) surface. The images give a clear view to the differences between the exposure of the clean surface to the adsorbates and the clean one itself. While the oxygen exposed surface shows defects and larger adsorbates, on the hydrogen exposed surface defects alter the contrast due to electronic effects and adsorbates remain invisible. Scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) provides information about the conduction band onsets.

articleTitle: Below-bandgap photoluminescence from GaAs
abstract: Below-bandgap photoluminescence (PL) from GaAs has been investigated. We find that various electronic states giving rise to near-infrared (NIR) PL peaks can be generated through processes that are standard for epitaxial growth of InAlGaAs structures on (001) GaAs substrates. The PL signals from these states overlap with those from InAs quantum dots, wetting layers, and InGaAs structures, complicating the design of devices for telecommunications or intermediate band solar cells. The present result provides guides for distinguishing the desired electronic states from the thermal treatment-induced defect states.

articleTitle: Reflectivity of hexagonal Boron-Nitride in deep UV
abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is one of the most promising materials for light emitting devices in the deep UV. hBN-bulk was demonstrated as an indirect band-gap semiconductor with an excitonic emission at 5.95 eV and phonon replicas between 5.7 and 5.9 eV. At lower energies emission bands comes from extended defects or stacking faults while the optical properties for the energy range higher than the fundamental band-gap are still under debate.

articleTitle: GaN HEMT Characterization for Base Stations
abstract: This paper describes characterization method for the current source of GaN HEMTs and its relation to the efficiency, optimal load impedance, and operating classes. We have demonstrated a time-domain measurement setup working at low-frequency (LF) is a powerful tool for accurate evaluation of the current source. Furthermore, this characterization method enables RF characteristics such as output power and drain efficiency on arbitrary different classes of operation.

articleTitle: Improved insulator/semiconductor interfaces in Al2O3/AlGaN/GaN structures by AlGaN layer regrowth
abstract: We investigated the effect of AlGaN regrown layer on the device characteristics of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AlGaN/GaN metal-oxide-semiconductor high-electron-mobility transistors (MOS-HEMTs). From capacitance-voltage (C-V) investigations, it was confirmed that the quality of the Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/AlGaN interfaces are improved by AlGaN regrowth as evidenced by negative shift of threshold voltage and the appearance of a second step in the C-V profile. Consequently, enhancement of transfer characteristic curves in terms of increased linearity and drain current density was also observed.

articleTitle: Heteroepitaxial growth of InGaAs/InP/InAlAs/InP core-multishell nanowires on Si for a complementary tunnel FETs
abstract: Tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) is promising millivolt switch for future logic applications. However, the steepness of the subthreshold slope (SS), that defines the power consumption, and low conductance are still challenges due to lack of moderate tunnel junction and the device design. And, complementary switching operation is serious problem for TFET logic application due to asymmetry junction in the TFETs. Here we propose a solution for these challenges by a heteroepitaxial growth of InGaAs-based core-multishell (CMS) nanowire (NW) on Si with surrounding-gate structure.

articleTitle: 2DEG formation in doped polytype InP nanowires: an optical study
abstract: One advantage of nanowires is the possibility to create heterostructures of the same material, but different crystal structures. These polytype-interfaces are atomically sharp and, in many cases, have a type-II band-alignment. We show, using optical methods, that n-type doped polytype InP nanowires form a 2D electron gas at the polytype-interfaces. Using the photoluminescence from doped and undoped polytype nanowires, we can estimate a lower bound for the band-offset of the type-II band-alignment.

articleTitle: High-Temperature Annealing of Sputter-Deposited AlN on Diamond Substrate
abstract: Diamond is an attractive widegap semiconductor for power devices due to the bandgap of 5.5 eV and high hole conductivity. Quantum sensing by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers has also been focused on in recent years. On the other hand, (Al, Ga)N has been extensively studied for deep ultraviolet LEDs and high electron mobility transistors, whereas the poor p-type conductance limits the performance of bipolar devices. Hence, the heterogeneous integration of diamond and (Al, Ga)N is expected to realize efficient carrier injection into widegap bipolar devices.

articleTitle: Effect of Annealing on The Bottom Cell in GaInP/GaAs/GaInNAsSb Triple Junction Solar Cells by MBE/MOCVD Hybrid Growth
abstract: This work focuses on the effect of annealing in the dilute nitride bottom subcell in the GaInP/GaAs/GaInNAsSb triple-junction (3J) solar cells fabricated by a hybrid growth of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). It is found that the effect on the improvement of carrier collection properties in the nip-GaInNAsSb solar cells depends if they have some upper subcell layers or not. Analyses of hydrogen depth profiles, carrier concentrations, and defects indicate that the unintentionally incorporated hydrogen is connected to degradation of the solar cell properties upon annealing.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Infrared Photo-responses of the Schottky Gate Region of an n-AlGaAs/GaAs Heterojunction FET by a Second Light Illumination
abstract: Infrared (IR) photo-responses of the Schottky-barrier gate region are investigated in an n-AlGaAs/GaAs field-effect transistor (FET). The photocurrent from the channel region to the gate is strongly enhanced by about 3.4 times when a weak second light having photon energy above the GaAs bandgap illuminates the FET locally. The enhancement effect is independent of the illumination position of the second light, and remains even when the position is far away from the gate region. The experimental results are compared with a theoretical model based on the electron drift and hole diffusion.

articleTitle: Halide Vapor Phase Epitaxy of $\alpha$-Ga2O3
